device_label: 8 mm SPH MZM, high-Tg side-chain polymer on 40 nm silicon strip
il_onchip_includes: about 12 mm of strip waveguide including the active phase shifter (scattering loss), per the authors
il_onchip_excludes: Y-junctions (about 1.4 dB in total) and lensed-fibre edge coupling (about 3 dB per facet)
electrode_metal: gold strip-line electrodes (signal line); aluminum bottom electrode, 1 um
substrate: silicon wafer with 2 um oxide and 1 um aluminum bottom electrode
cladding: sol-gel SiO2, 3 um top and 3 um bottom
epitaxy_or_stack: Layer stack bottom to top: silicon wafer with 2 um oxide; 1 um aluminum bottom electrode; 3 um sol-gel SiO2; 40 nm PECVD silicon strip core, 4 um wide, e-beam patterned and SF6 ICP etched; 1 um side-chain EO polymer layer; 3 um sol-gel SiO2; gold strip-line electrodes 8 mm long. TM0 mode, polymer index 1.67, silicon index 3.48, confinement factor in polymer 73.8 percent (simulated, Supplementary Note 1).
modulation_format: OOK 90, 100, 110, 120 Gbit/s (no error floor down to BER 1e-5 for 90-110 Gbit/s); PAM4 88, 104, 112 Gbit/s (44-56 GBd); Nyquist PAM4 160, 184, 200 Gbit/s (80, 92, 100 GBd, roll-off 0.01)
driver: OOK: SHF 12104A pattern generator with SHF 2:1 multiplexer and RF amplifier, 2.0 Vpp; PAM4: Keysight M8196A AWG (92 GSa/s) or M8194A AWG (120 GSa/s, Nyquist) with SHF S804B linear driver, 1.3 Vpp; RF probe, 50 ohm termination
notes: Single device; numbers from the Nature Communications version of record, its Supplementary Information and the Author Correction (Fig. 1c label 4 mm -> 4 um; no value changes). Vpi 1.8 V comes from Table 1 and equals the measured Vpi*L of 1.44 V cm at 1.55 um over the 8 mm arm; frequency, wavelength sweep and drive convention of the Vpi measurement are not stated (text calls Vpi a static parameter), so vpi_convention and drive stay unspecified. The two 8 mm arms are 200 um apart (p.3); two gold strip lines (Fig. 1b) are fed by a single G-S-G probe (Fig. 1d); how the arms are driven is not stated. Two source statements bear on the drive form but neither names it: Methods p.7 (Energy consumption) says "with dual-drive configuration, the energy consumption could be further reduced", implying the measured device was not dual-drive; Supplementary Note 2 (p.3-4) defines the half-wave voltage as the voltage producing a phase shift of pi and Eq. 5.b uses a single phase-shifter length L with no push-pull factor of 2, so the 1021 pm/V extraction (r33 223 pm/V) assumes the full pi over one 8 mm length. With the single G-S-G feed and vertical poling against a common bottom electrode this points to single-arm operation, but the authors do not state it; drive and vpi_convention stay unspecified. Bandwidth: measured 3 dB EO bandwidth around 68 GHz read on a VNA limited to 70 GHz (Fig. 1f; fitted line, ripple up to about +1 dB above the 0 dB start); normalisation frequency not stated (low_freq_unstated); the 6 dB bandwidth is only presumed over 70 GHz and is not entered. Loss (Supplementary Note 5): fiber-to-fiber loss about 10 dB = about 3 dB per facet lensed-fibre edge coupling x 2, Y-junctions about 1.4 dB, and about 2.6 dB on-chip waveguide/phase-shifter loss, which with a 12 mm total device length gives the 0.22 dB/mm (2.2 dB/cm) propagation loss, also stated as confirmed on a straight reference waveguide (not shown). Main text gives no insertion loss. Electrode: gold strip line 16 um wide, 3 um thick over a bottom aluminium electrode, G-S-G probe pads (Fig. 1d); Z0 is a design target matched to 50 ohm (Supplementary Note 3, CST FEM, close to 50 ohm over 20-200 GHz, no value) not a measured impedance; electrode_type other because no enum fits; n_RF not reported (text says refractive indices of microwave and light are comparable). In-device n^3 r33 = 1021 pm/V at 1.55 um; Supplementary Note 2 / Table 1 give in-device r33 = 223 pm/V with n = 1.66 (derived by the authors from Vpi*L = 1.44 V cm, confinement 0.738, d_eo 1 um, d_c 6 um, eps about 3; the main text quotes polymer index 1.67 from the modal calculation), Tg 172 C, poling 300-400 V near Tg. Energy per bit: authors compute Wbit = (Vpp/2)^2/(B R) (load energy only, not driver); 42 fJ/bit is the 200 Gbit/s Nyquist PAM4 point at 1.3 Vpp and 50 ohm (drive_vpp_v 1.3, reference plane not stated); the same formula gives 151 fJ/bit at 56 Gbit/s OOK, 1.3 Vpp and about 200 fJ/bit at 100 Gbit/s OOK, 2.0 Vpp. Data: 100 Gbit/s OOK eye Q 7.3, 120 Gbit/s OOK Q 5.4 (Fig. 2); 160 and 184 Gbit/s Nyquist PAM4 below pre-HD-FEC (3.8e-3) and pre-KP4-FEC (2.2e-4), 200 Gbit/s below pre-HD-FEC only (Fig. 3g). Temperature (not separate rows, only link performance was measured at 25-110 C): OOK 56 Gbit/s Q drops under 0.5 dB, 100 and 110 Gbit/s under 2.5 dB; 200 Gbit/s PAM4 BER rises under one order of magnitude 22-110 C; 100 Gbit/s BER curves show negligible penalty after 100 h at 90 C (Figs. 4, 5; Supplementary Fig. 4). temperature_class and temperature_k left empty because the static Vpi and bandwidth temperatures are not stated. Internal inconsistency: loss-efficiency product 3.6 V dB in the text (p.6) but 3.2 V dB in Table 1 (p.7); 0.22 dB/mm x 14.4 V mm gives about 3.2 V dB. Source inconsistency: the Keysight M8196A AWG sampling rate is 92 GSa/s in the text (p.3, p.8 Methods) but the Fig. 3a setup label (p.5) reads "96 or 120 GSa/s"; driver follows the body text. Not entered: loss-efficiency product, BVR (38 GHz/V), Tg, confinement factor.

device_label: 23.5 mm DP-IQ, four sub-MZMs with CL-TWE (130 GBd PCS-400QAM)
cladding: SiO2 0.7 um under the electrodes; air above
epitaxy_or_stack: x-cut TFLN device layer 360 nm on 500 um quartz; 0.7 um SiO2; 0.9 um Au CL-TWE
modulation_format: DP-PCS-400QAM at 130 GBd, entropy 8.14-8.54 bit/symbol/pol; 8.44 bit/symbol/pol: pre-FEC BER 1.91e-2, SNR 23.4 dB, information rate 15.38 bit/symbol
driver: SiGe DAC at 130 GSa/s (overclocked), no driver amplifier stated
notes: Single row for the four sub-MZMs (XI, XQ, YI, YQ), all stated to give Vpi 1 V and 3 dB EO bandwidth above 110 GHz; the paper gives no per-channel numbers, statistic left empty. More than five DP-IQ modulators on the same chip all show about 110 GHz, 1 V, optical loss 6.5 dB +/- 0.5 dB (unqualified "optical loss", not entered) and ER above 20 dB. Vpi: Fig. 1(f) transmission sweep, measurement frequency and wavelength not stated; push-pull and MZM-level convention inferred from the x-cut two-arm CL-TWE layout, authors do not state it. vpil_dc_vcm is left empty: the only stated VpiL is the simulated design efficiency 2.4 V cm (text p.2), not a measured device value; 1 V x 2.35 cm gives 2.35 V cm (derived by the build step); vpi_dc_v is measured. Bandwidth: Fig. 1(g) traces end near 110 GHz at about -3 dB; text states >110 GHz for all channels (100 GHz photodetector, VNA with frequency converters, 1.5 GHz reference); a model fit extrapolates the 3 dB point beyond 140 GHz (not entered). ER above 20 dB is stated for all sub-MZMs without naming static or dynamic; the Fig. 1(f) sweep minimum reads about 0.03-0.05 of the maximum (about 13-15 dB) on one unspecified sub-MZM. Fiber-to-fiber loss 6.8 dB includes polarization-independent edge couplers at 1.9 dB per facet and the PRC (below 0.3 dB, polarization ER at least 20.5 dB, 1520-1580 nm). Wavelength of the modulator measurements not stated (PRC characterised over C band only), so band is empty. Drive 0.628 Vpp is stated at the sub-MZMs after cable and probe-array loss (RMS 161 mV). 1.96 Tb/s is the net rate with a 10 percent spatially-coupled LDPC FEC at 8.44 bit/symbol/pol; line rate not stated. 1.04 fJ/bit stated in the conclusion without formula or scope. Simulated RF loss 0.21 dB/cm/GHz^0.5 and perfect velocity matching are design statements, not entered; 50 ohm flip-chip terminators are not a measured Z0. CL-TWE dimensions (Fig. 1(b)): period 50 um, segment gap c 5 um, s 1 um, t 1 um, ws 80 um (the arrow spans the light region between the inner edges of the two segment rows in Fig. 1(b), not a stated signal-conductor width; not entered; by the 50 um scale bar the arm pitch is about 104 um). Electrode gap 3 um and rib top width 2.5 um from Fig. 1(c) and text. buffer_oxide_um 0.7 is the text value ("0.7-um-thick SiO2 cladding", p.2); in Fig. 1(c) the 0.7 um arrows may instead span the electrode bottom to the quartz top (alternative reading: about 0.52 um SiO2 over the slab), not adopted.
